correctness.finding: The original numeric pair was wrong because it identified the discrete coupling with the difference of conditional per-cut cubic means. In the multi-cut fluctuation formula the coupling is the filling derivative of the equilibrium statistic. For the symmetric genus-one curve the normalized filling variation gives c0=4π/f_A=15.1709297058687..., yielding corrected limits 20.28718707889796... and 75.71281292110204.... The qualitative even/odd nonconvergence survives.

originality.finding: Borot–Guionnet and Shcherbina supply the general oscillatory multi-cut theory, including the filling-fraction mechanism, but the targeted comparison did not locate this explicit corrected evaluation for Tr M^3 at V=x^4/4-2x^2. The repair narrows originality to the reference-point evaluation rather than the general theorem.

scientific_value.finding: After correction, the record gives a concrete and reproducible reference value for a genuine multi-cut parity oscillation with a large subsequential gap. This is useful as a benchmark for implementations of multi-cut fluctuation formulae, provided the result is presented as an explicit evaluation rather than a new general phenomenon.

independent_checks: independently recomputed f_A, f_B, t, q, the zero-A-period kernel constant and the discrete even/odd theta variances at high precision
derived the filling response from the normalized holomorphic differential and its expansion at infinity, obtaining c0=4π/f_A
recomputed the corrected v_even, v_odd and their gap and verified the qualitative nonconvergence remains
compared the coupling with Borot–Guionnet multi-cut filling-fraction/linear-statistic structure and Shcherbina quasi-periodic variance theory
confirmed the current main record tree matches the assigned source-tree SHA
limitations: High-precision quadrature is not a formal interval proof, although the 55.4 gap is far larger than numerical uncertainty.
The general multi-cut asymptotic theorem is cited rather than rederived.
Open-access full text was sufficient; Oxford Download was not needed.
